verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission has successfully launched as of April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Artemis II crew blasted off on their lunar journey from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday.' (April 1, 2026); R4: 'Launch date April 1, 2026'; R5: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 6:35 p.m. ET.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm successful launch on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed mission to the moon in more than 50 years'; R2: 'first time since 1972'; R3: 'first time in more than 50 years'; R4: 'first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972.'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state this milestone.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Mr. Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, as well as Jeremy Hansen'; identical in others.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew listed in all sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission duration is ~10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day mission'; R2: '10-day mission'; R4: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes and 15 seconds' (~10 days).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission involves testing the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey'; R2: 'first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R4: 'validate the Orion spacecraft's systems'.
verifications.reasoning: Directly described as test flight for Orion.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of the Artemis II mission, the spacecraft will return to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10'; R4: 'Landing date April 11, 2026' (day 10 elapsed).

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of the Artemis II mission, there will be testing of the heat shield against temperatures near 2,700°C (4,900°F).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'expected to splashdown... on April 10'; 'testing of the heat shield'; R5: 'face temperatures of 3,000 degrees on re-entry'.
verifications.reasoning: Reentry on day 10 tests heat shield at high temps (~5000F/2700C approximate), but exact figure/temperature not precisely matched.
